---
title: "check-extracted-lemmas.yml"
---

Diff-scoped, warn-only heuristic check for the lab's rule (Ezra, 2026-10-29)
to extract a lemma wherever feasible:
a general fact that does not depend on its setting
goes in its own `#lem-` div, on the site that owns the topic,
and the proof, solution or example that uses it links to the lemma.

The check reads the body of

- each `#sol-` and `#exm-` div, and
- the proof of each `#thm-`, `#lem-`, `#cor-` or `#prp-` div
  (a `.proof` div nested in it or directly after it).

A body is flagged when a sentence of its prose says
"for any", "for every" or "for all"
and also holds inline math,
and the body cites no result
(`@thm-`, `@lem-`, `@cor-`, `@prp-`,
or a link to a `#thm-`, `#lem-`, `#cor-` or `#prp-` anchor).
A theorem's own statement is not read, since a theorem is meant to be general.
The check follows `{{< include >}}` lines,
so it reads a page in the order a reader sees it.
A body that holds `<!-- lemma-ok: reason -->` is exempt.

A body is checked when the pull request adds a line inside it.
With no base to diff against, the check skips instead of scanning the whole tree,
so existing content is fixed when someone edits it anyway.
It warns by default; `fail: true` blocks.

## Inputs

| Input | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `globs` | `*.qmd` | Git pathspecs of tracked files to check (recursive) |
| `paths-ignore` | none | Comma or newline separated globs to skip |
| `fail` | `false` | Fail on a finding; `false` warns |
| `whole-tree` | `false` | Check every body, to measure a corpus |
| `python-version` | `3.x` | Python version |
| `runs-on` | empty (`CI_RUNNER` variable, else `ubuntu-latest`) | Runner label; a self-hosted label only for a private repository |

## Usage

Copy `examples/check-extracted-lemmas.yml` to
`.github/workflows/check-extracted-lemmas.yml`.
